findings.what: publish() freezes an entry once status is set, but loggingFetch sets status before it reads the body. A publish in that gap leaves responseBody null in every later snapshot.
findings.why: In src/web/app/data/api.ts:440-442, loggingFetch sets entry.status, then awaits response.clone().text(), then sets responseBody. publish() keeps a shallow copy taken at the first publish where status was non-null (browser.ts:25). If another request starts or settles while this body is still being read, the copy holds status and headers but responseBody null, and the final publish keeps that stale copy for good. Two things break. The request log then shows no response body for an exchange that had one, which breaks WB-7 ('the exact request and response') and HONEST-1. The policy view's sale match, responseBody.includes(reference) at PolicyView.tsx:340, also drops the POST that created the policy. This node introduced the regression for acceptance line 12. wb-7-log-growth.test.tsx only sends requests one after another, so it can't see the race. A settled exchange has to be one whose body has also been read, and a test should cover two exchanges in flight at once.
